scope: Final-sweep-only membership inventory optimization; no Lean/compiler/checker or test process launched by reviewer
findings: No blocking guard regression found in reviewed revision.
Sorted snapshot names and bisect prefix enumeration reproduce existing .olean* and .ir* file membership for MODULE-valid artifact names, including prefix overlaps and exotic regular sidecars.
Only the final successful sweep supplies the snapshot; it follows ThreadPoolExecutor.shutdown(wait=True). Active builds, publication and resume retain live artifact_files enumeration.
All prior runtime, source, accepted receipt, compiler log, dependency and bundle Pins.verify calls remain. Expected content hashes are not replaced by snapshot metadata.
Snapshot covers the entire artifact tree, all directories and regular files, including files outside any selected bundle prefix. Symlinks and special files now fail closed in this phase.

Directory enumeration has before/after metadata checks, followed by per-entry metadata rechecks. A second whole-tree snapshot must exactly match all directory/file identities and membership before success is written.
Source changes imply a distinct runner/build identity; old-origin receipts cannot be silently resumed. Separately pinned audit/checker wrappers need explicit reviewed pin changes.
limits: Static review is not a Lean theorem proof or a full-project performance measurement.
Original15 fake lifecycle fixture report is owner-supplied evidence; A mutation-fixture report was still pending at this review timestamp.
File identity checks rely on ordinary filesystem device/inode/mode/size/mtime/ctime behavior and coordinated nonhostile writers. They are not a hostile-filesystem security boundary.
The change preserves existing source/runtime guard scheduling; it does not assert a globally atomic filesystem snapshot or eliminate the final check-to-summary interval.
